summary: Round 2 of M4.9. The two round-1 blockers are structurally addressed and the production change itself is sound: the retracted 'MUST NOT CALL IT WITH ITS OWN epoch' claim survives nowhere in the tree (grepped, only its own retraction remains); the CheckpointCursor extraction is a byte-for-byte move with call sites renamed and no assertion weakened; ADR-0035's decision table (28->30, 56->58, 20->22, 47->52), its 'GETs unchanged at 18 and 46' claim and its 'one stat per takeover plus one per ancestor' arithmetic all reproduce exactly; the neverOpened-branch probe cannot terminate a walk that should continue (a checkpoint only exists on a chain that was opened, and its offsets are cumulative); and the full suite is green. One major finding: ADR-0035's 'What the new budget buys' baseline is not the baseline. Using this commit's own takeoverCost harness -- calibrated, because it reproduces the new figure of 17 exactly -- the same fixture on HEAD (15da3fb, M4.8c) costs 29/46/80/148/284 total at 1/2/4/8/16 prior terms, not the 26/43/77/145/281 the ADR records as MEASURED, and stats grow 4/5/7/11/19, not the 3/4/6/10/18 stated (that series is the LIST series, duplicated). The slopes match exactly, so the shape claim is true and the win is in fact LARGER than the ADR claims; the numbers are stale, not the conclusion. The remedy is three number corrections in prose (ADR-0035, backlog-done M4.9, LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest's class javadoc) -- this is NOT a commit that needs splitting under review.md rule two-round-cap, and if a third round is unwanted the fix is a docs-only edit or a staged rounds:M4.9 argument. Answering the four questions asked: (1) the rewritten CheckpointCursor javadoc is true in every clause except a broken {@link #replayAncestry} reference and one retained pre-M4.9 forward-looking paragraph; (2) ADR-0035 is honest on the move and stale on the baseline, and its rejected-alternative section cites a test that does not in fact pin what it says; (3) the neverOpened probe is correct but reachable by no test; (4) the CheckpointCursor split is real, the test split is only half done -- the cost suite still carries its own copy of the whole fixture.

findings.rule: cost.md R18; non-negotiable 4 (never claim a number was measured without having done it)
findings.location: ## What the new budget buys; repeated in docs/internal/product/backlog-done.md M4.9 and sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest.java class javadoc
findings.title: The pre-change baseline quoted as MEASURED does not reproduce on the tree this change was made against; the stat series is the LIST series duplicated
findings.detail: The ADR states: '17 total requests at one prior term and 17 at sixteen -- GETs 5, LISTs 3 at both -- against 26/43/77/145/281 at 1/2/4/8/16 terms before, with LISTs and stats each growing 3/4/6/10/18.' I re-measured with the commit's own takeoverCost fixture (K injected at 1, frozen renew and checkpoint tickers, CountingBinStore wrapping both the store and the LeaseManager, next.close() counted). Calibration: on the staged tree it yields StoreCounts[puts=4, gets=5, lists=3, stats=5] = 17 at every term count, exactly as claimed -- so the harness is the right one. Running the identical harness on HEAD (15da3fb, M4.8c -- the tree this change was authored against) gives puts=4, gets=18, lists=3, stats=4 = 29 at one prior term, and 4/243/18/19 = 284 at sixteen; the full series is 29/46/80/148/284, GETs 18/33/63/123/243, LISTs 3/4/6/10/18, stats 4/5/7/11/19. Reproduced identically at 537cfbf (M4.8b2), and at 28/45/79/147/283 if next.close() is excluded from the count -- so no close-counting convention yields 26. The first differences (17/34/68/136) are identical between the recorded series and the measured one, so this is a constant offset from an older tree, not a different fixture. Two consequences. (a) 26 is not the number: the honest comparison is 17 against 29, i.e. the bound buys MORE than the ADR claims. (b) 'LISTs and stats each growing 3/4/6/10/18' is wrong for stats -- the true stat series is 4/5/7/11/19, and the quoted one is the LIST series written twice, which is the signature of transcription rather than measurement. Failure scenario: this ADR is, by cost.md R18, the durable record authorising a budget move, and the backlog row calls itself 'the evidence carrying a non-negotiable-2 exception'. A later task re-measures the uncheckpointed crossing, reads 29 against the recorded 26, and either reports a three-request regression that never happened or -- the dangerous direction -- absorbs a genuine three-request regression because the new measurement now matches the recorded baseline. The same row already carried one round of wrong MEASURED figures and records that it was 'corrected by re-measuring'; the re-measurement produced these. Answering the question put to me directly: quoting 17 against 26 is not a comparison of different fixtures -- it is the same fixture against a stale tree, and the fix is to replace 26/43/77/145/281 with 29/46/80/148/284 and the stat series with 4/5/7/11/19 in all three places.
findings.remedy: Correct the four figures in ADR-0035 § What the new budget buys, in the backlog-done M4.9 row, and in the LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest class javadoc. No code change.
findings.failure_scenario: A later task re-measures the uncheckpointed takeover crossing on this same fixture, reads 29 requests at one prior term against ADR-0035's recorded 26, and either files a three-request regression that never happened -- or, in the dangerous direction, absorbs a genuine three-request regression because the new measurement now matches the recorded baseline exactly. The ADR is the artifact cost.md R18 makes the durable record of a budget move, so it is what that comparison will be made against.

findings.title: The fix for round 1's minor is reached by no test: deleting the neverOpened-branch probe leaves the whole suite green
findings.detail: Surviving mutation, measured: delete both statements of `if (chainEpoch >= 1 && crossFromCheckpoint(hops, chainEpoch, limit)) { break; }` from the neverOpened branch, leaving the arithmetic hop as it was before this round. `./gradlew :sequencer:test` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL. The branch itself is reached (neverOpened's own javadoc cites the two-consecutive-failed-takeovers fixture), but never with a checkpoint present anywhere in the ancestry, so crossFromCheckpoint always returns false and the added call is indistinguishable from its absence. The sibling in-loop probe on the CONTINUE branch got a test this round (aPredecessorTOOSHORTToCheckpointStillStopsAtItsAncestorsCheckpoint, which I confirmed is a real discriminator: 26 actual, 30 asserted, 86 with that probe deleted); the neverOpened one did not. Failure scenario: a future refactor of the burned-epoch arithmetic drops the probe and nothing anywhere notices, restoring exactly the behaviour round 1 asked to be fixed -- a run of burned epochs replaying the first genuinely opened chain in full with its checkpoint unread. The shape a test needs is a burned epoch (a chain sealed at slot 0, or empty) sitting above a checkpointed term, entered through a CONTINUE that names the burned epoch. I am not asking for it in this round; recording it so it is not lost.
findings.remedy: Either add the fixture, or say in the commit body that this branch is unpinned and why, so the next reader does not assume the suite protects it.
findings.failure_scenario: A future refactor of the burned-epoch arithmetic in replayAncestry drops the neverOpened-branch probe; every test in the tree stays green; and a takeover that reaches the first genuinely opened chain across a run of burned epochs replays that chain in full with its checkpoint sitting unread -- the exact behaviour round 1 asked to be fixed, silently restored.

findings.title: The cost/correctness split does not share the shared fixture -- it duplicates it
findings.detail: The backlog row and the fixture's own javadoc say the suite 'splits into COST and CORRECTNESS around a shared fixture'. BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest does static-import PREFIX, RA, frozen, manager, noRenew, request and streamOfTerm from BoundedRecoveryFixture. LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest imports none of them: it declares its own PREFIX, TTL, RENEW, A, RA, TestClock, manager(), frozen(), noRenew(), both request() overloads and streamOfTerm(), byte-identical to the fixture's. Failure scenario, already realised once in this very diff: the change from `LocalSequencer.sleepFor(RENEW)` to a frozen `noRenew()` -- made because the real renew ticker inside a counting window is 'a latent flake rather than a safe one' -- had to be applied twice, and a future edit to the fixture (a second stream in request(), a different PREFIX, a real clock) will silently apply to the correctness assertions and not to the request-count assertions, after which the two suites measure different things while claiming to measure two halves of one. Two leftovers make the half-done state visible: BoundedRecoveryFixture ends with an orphan javadoc for takeoverCost, a method that lives in the other file, attached to nothing; and LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest retains four imports it no longer uses (binjava.format.Checkpoint, Checkpoint.StreamOffsets, binjava.binstore.Body, java.io.IOException) from the tests that moved out.
findings.remedy: Have LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest static-import the fixture as the correctness suite does, move takeoverCost into BoundedRecoveryFixture under the javadoc that already describes it, and drop the four dead imports.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone edits BoundedRecoveryFixture.request() to commit a second stream, or changes PREFIX, believing both bounded-recovery suites share it. Only the correctness suite changes. The cost suite's request-count assertions keep passing against a fixture that no longer matches, so the two halves of the split measure different workloads while claiming to be the cost and correctness halves of one. This already happened once inside this diff: the sleepFor(RENEW) to noRenew() change had to be made in both files by hand.

findings.title: The rejected alternative names a test that does not refuse it
findings.detail: The ADR says skipping the own-epoch probe is rejected because `CommitLog.recover()` on a chain with its own checkpoint 'would go back to unbounded, which is precisely the shape recoveringAChainThatCheckpointedItsOWNProgressKeepsItsNextSequence pins'. Measured: guarding the first-hop probe with `epoch != ownEpoch` -- which is exactly that variant, since inherited() passes ownEpoch = Long.MIN_VALUE and so keeps its probe -- leaves that named test PASSING. It has to: a full replay of the own chain derives the same nextSequence from the entries it reads, which is what the test asserts. What actually fails is aCheckpointSittingEXACTLYOnTheBarrierIsUsed (total 18 becomes 17, the new absolute cost assertion) and LocalSequencerFailoverTest's four totals. The substantive objection -- that the own-chain path loses its bound, correcting the earlier 'assumption about callers' draft -- is right; only the citation is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that makes the rejection look better pinned than it is. Failure scenario: someone removing the own-epoch stat to save a request checks the cited test, sees it green, and concludes the ADR's own objection has evaporated.
findings.remedy: Cite aCheckpointSittingEXACTLYOnTheBarrierIsUsed's absolute total, or say plainly that what refuses this variant is a cost assertion rather than a correctness one.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone proposing to drop the own-epoch stat to save a request per takeover reads the ADR's rejection, runs the test it names -- recoveringAChainThatCheckpointedItsOWNProgressKeepsItsNextSequence -- watches it pass under the change, and concludes the recorded objection no longer applies. Measured: that test does pass under `epoch != ownEpoch && crossFromCheckpoint(...)`; what fails is a cost assertion the ADR does not mention.

findings.title: Two residues in the rewritten javadoc: a {@link} that cannot resolve, and a paragraph still written from before M4.9
findings.detail: The retraction paragraph is otherwise true in every clause I checked -- the fresh epoch, the empty own chain at a takeover, the first-hop probe being what bounds inherited(), and the own-epoch stat bounding CommitLog.recover() -- and the retracted claim exists nowhere else in the tree (grepped for 'MUST NOT CALL', 'its own epoch' and 'returns EMPTY at every takeover' across every .java and .md; only ADR-0034's neighbours and this retraction come back). Two residues. (a) It says 'M4.9 does, deliberately: {@link #replayAncestry} probes the epoch it is given BEFORE walking'. `#replayAncestry` names a member of CheckpointCursor, which has none; the method is ChainReplay's, and private. The reference resolves for a human and not for javadoc, which is the same class of drift the round-1 finding was about. (b) The retained paragraph ending 'M4.9 needs a bound on the WALK, not only on the replay' is written from a pre-M4.9 vantage inside the commit that delivers M4.9. Its arithmetic remains true of the UNCHECKPOINTED path, so it is not false -- but a maintainer reads it as open work in the file that closed it, which is the same trap the round-1 finding described.
findings.remedy: Point the link at ChainReplay (or spell the method out in {@code}), and re-tense the last paragraph to say what still holds -- one stat per ancestor on an ancestry with no checkpoint -- rather than what M4.9 still needs.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer opening CheckpointCursor to change the discovery mechanism reads the closing paragraph as an open requirement on M4.9 -- 'M4.9 needs a bound on the WALK' -- in the file that already carries that bound, and either re-does the work or concludes the commit is unfinished. Separately, a javadoc build (or an IDE navigation) cannot resolve {@link #replayAncestry}, so the sentence that justifies the own-epoch probe points at nothing checkable.
